thread:
devon harris: Hi team — I was on an approved medical leave during open enrollment and just returned. I missed the enrollment window. Is there any way to enroll in medical/dental now? I have the approval docs for the leave and can provide dates. Also wondering about HSA eligibility if allowed midyear.

erin (People Ops): Welcome back, @devon — hope you're doing better. Short answer: missing open enrollment while on approved leave can qualify for a special enrollment exception in some cases. Upload the leave approval and any relevant HR notices to the benefits portal and choose "Open Enrollment Exception" as the reason: https://benefits.redwood.com/forms/exception-request. We review these on a case-by-case basis.

people-ops-bot: Reminder: open enrollment exceptions require documentation and manager/HR verification. Submission does not guarantee approval; carriers and plan rules may limit retroactive additions. See policy: https://benefits.redwood.com/open-enroll-exceptions :information_source:

sara (Benefits): Adding detail: if the exception is approved, coverage effective date depends on the reason and carrier rules. For leave-related exceptions we typically allow an effective date back to the date your leave began or the date you returned, depending on documentation and carrier flexibility. Payroll will prorate premiums from the chosen effective date and may process a retro deduction or credit on the next paycheck. HSA: if enrolled in an HSA-eligible plan midyear, your HSA eligibility and contribution limits are governed by IRS rules — pro rata contributions apply and we can project annual limits for you.

erin (People Ops): Practical tips: 1) include the HR leave approval email, FMLA/short-term disability paperwork if any, and your manager's confirmation of leave dates. 2) indicate whether you want medical + dental and whether you'd like HSA. 3) If you need coverage retro to the open enrollment effective date, note that carriers sometimes deny retro coverage beyond a certain window; we'll flag that in the review.

devon harris: Thanks — uploading docs now. If approved, can I ask to spread any retro premium over two paychecks? I get that payroll might do a single adjustment; prefer two smaller hits.

sara (Benefits): Yes, we can request payroll split for retro deductions in most cases. Put that preference in the exception form notes and we'll route to payroll ops with the case. If you expect a big retro amount, we can also explore an alternate effective date to reduce the immediate hit (carrier permitting).

erin (People Ops): Got the upload, @devon. We'll review and aim to update you within 5 business days. If carriers require additional evidence, we'll follow up. Glad to have you back. :handshake:
